Iran’s Infrastructure : the US Promised To Use Heavy Bombers

🔠🔠🔠🔠1️⃣

Trump threatened Wednesday to bomb one Iranian bridge or power plant in return for each attack on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, reiterating his longstanding threat to go after Iranian infrastructure as fighting has escalated in recent weeks and could reportedly further intensify in the coming days.

Disputes over management of the strait led to the collapse of a preliminary deal between the United States and Iran, and both sides have exchanged daily fire across the Middle East and threatened to escalate the conflict even further.

According to a Wednesday report in Hebrew media, the US informed Israel that it will soon deploy heavy bombers for strikes on Iran, presumably targeting fortified nuclear sites, in what would be a major escalation.

“Any time the Islamic Republic of Iran shoots at a ship in the Strait of Hormuz, whether it be by Missile, Rocket, Drone, or any other device or weapon, the United States will bomb and destroy ONE BRIDGE OR POWER PLANT,” Trump wrote on social media.

In response to Trump’s threat to Iran’s infrastructure, an Iranian military source cited by Tasnim news agency said Tehran would retaliate against infrastructure in the region.

Iran’s top negotiator Mohammad Ghalibaf expanded on the threats, saying no one will be able to sell oil in a region where Iran is not able to do so, and adding that if Tehran’s security is not ensured, no infrastructure will be safe.

“The equation of this war is clear: either all or none,” Ghalibaf said in a post on X.

“Our defense doctrine is clear: eye for an eye. Any aggression against Iran, including our infrastructure, will compel a powerful and decisive response,” Foreign Minister Araghchi wrote on X.

In addition, Iran’s state broadcaster quoted the military as saying that US threats “will have no result other than the expansion of the war.”

Iran on Wednesday fired missiles and drones at several Arab regional countries, including at Jordan’s Red Sea port of Aqaba, the interceptions of which could be heard in Israel’s southern city of Eilat.

Missile alerts also sounded in Kuwait and Bahrain. The Iranian military said it targeted US assets in both small Gulf countries, including air defense systems, radar installations and administrative buildings.

🖥 Tehran condemns UK decision to grant US access to military bases, says Britain complicit in aggression

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iran’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs has condemned Britain’s decision to grant the United States access to British military bases and infrastructure for strikes against the Islamic Republic, declaring this action a clear violation of the UN Charter and international law, which makes the European country complicit in the aggression against Iran.

In a statement released Thursday, the ministry referenced UN General Assembly Resolution 3314, which defines acts of aggression. It argued that by facilitating US and Israeli military operations, London has abandoned its responsibilities as a permanent member of the UN Security Council.
​
According to the statement, any participation or cooperation in the preparation and execution of these attacks constitutes complicity in the aggression and war crimes.
​
Tehran further asserted that this alliance invalidates the UK’s long-standing claims of upholding international law, human rights, and global security. The statement invoked a history of British interventionism in Iran, citing the 1953 coup, historical support for the Iraqi Baath regime during the 1980-1988 war on Iran, and various sanction regimes, as evidence of a recurring policy of hostility against the Iranian nation.
​
“The Islamic Republic of Iran is determined to defend its national sovereignty, territorial integrity, interests and national security against any aggression, and any party that, in any way, participates in military aggression against Iran will be responsible for the consequences and repercussions of its decision,” the ministry emphasized.
​
Bloomberg reported on Wednesday that new British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has authorized the US use of UK facilities, including RAF Fairford and Diego Garcia, for operations described by London as “defensive.”
​
While former Prime Minister Keir Starmer initiated the policy, Burnham’s approval has sparked internal dissent within the Labour Party. Anti-war lawmakers and opposition parties have warned that providing logistical support renders the UK directly complicit in the conflict.

The four documents cover road freight transportation, the construction of the Khosravi–Khanaqin–Baghdad railway, the establishment of a sister-city relationship between Tehran and Baghdad, and cooperation in public administration, training and human resources management.
